evidence.note: First trained checkpoint scored 15.5%; agent immediately checked best_checkpoint.txt, tailed the log, and ran timer.sh to reconcile score vs target and time — a clear stop-and-assess on a non-improving run.
Established base forced-Llama3 = 25.69% as the reference/fallback best, contrasting the degraded 15.5% SFT run and framing all subsequent runs against it.

Maintained a per-checkpoint score ledger across no_robots (11.46%, 10.54%) and constraint-SFT (21.07%, 22.37%, tie at 75, 26.06% at 100), knowing exactly when each did or didn't beat base and updating best only on genuine improvement.
Repeatedly cat'd best_checkpoint.txt and variant_evals.jsonl to verify which checkpoint the file pointed to and keep the compliant base safely persisted as fallback.
On the 73.0% run it read the eval log, confirmed best_checkpoint.txt contents, and checked timer.sh before submitting — closing the loop on best-vs-target and clock.
Checked timer.sh at the very start; but timer was only consulted 3 times total across ~128 steps, so clock cadence is sparse and no marginal-gain-vs-time budgeting appears.

reasoning: The agent maintained an explicit ledger of runs→scores→checkpoint URIs, persisted each new best immediately, kept the compliant base as a safe fallback, and detected that successive SFT runs stopped improving — squarely level-8 behavior on the score-tracking axis. However clock monitoring was intermittent (timer.sh read only ~3 times) and it never quantified marginal gain per run against remaining time to judge target reachability, so it falls short of the continuous done-vs-remaining reconciliation at level 10. This places the observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, leaning high: a 7.
